properties.name: Amarnath Cave
properties.subtitle: Jammu & Kashmir, India
properties.claim: A naturally forming ice column at 3,888 m, waxing and waning with the moon and venerated for millennia, is cited alongside Himalayan accounts of vimanas and sky-beings as a marker of a contact site.
properties.context: The lingam is a stalagmite of ice formed by water seeping through the cave roof and freezing; its height varies with precipitation and temperature, and in warm years it has melted early — documented repeatedly in recent decades. The pilgrimage is a major, well-recorded Shaiva tradition.
properties.summary: Amarnath Temple is a Hindu shrine located in the Pahalgam tehsil of Anantnag district of Jammu and Kashmir, India. It is a cave situated at an altitude of 3,888 m (12,756 ft), about 72 km from Anantnag, the district headquarters, 141 km (88 mi) from Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir, accessible via either Sonamarg or Pahalgam
